newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skandia reiterates to look at AFS future.
newsitem.headline: Skandia reiterates to look at AFS future.

text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia AB reiterated on Friday that it would look into the future of its fund operations Assurance & Financial Services, AFS.
"We will look into AFS's future, but nothing is said about any restructuring, sale or listing of the company," Skandia spokesman Anders Lundblad told Reuters.
A Friday article in domestic financial daily Dagens Industri said Skandia was preparing to list AFS.
"Our task is to turn AFS into a legal unit that Skandia could keep or sell," AFS president Jan Carendi was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
In the case of a possible bourse introduction, the New York bourse or other foreign bourses would be more likely than the Stockholm Stock Exchange, Carendi told the newspaper.
But he pointed out that it had not been decided if AFS would be listed at all.
Carendi's preference of the New York bourse over Stockholm's does not reflect Skandia's opinions, Lundblad said.

"This is Jan's personal opinion," Lundblad said. "Skandia has said that we will look into AFS's future...one alternative is a bourse introduction, another to continue as we do today. Nothing is decided and there is no time plan."
